shortDescription: Greece's manufacturing sector expanded in August at its strongest pace since March as new orders grew faster, a business survey showed on Tuesday.

children: Greece's manufacturing sector expanded in August at its strongest pace since March as new orders grew faster, a business survey showed on Tuesday.
The S&P Global Greece Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 54.4 in August from 54.3 in July. The 50 mark separates growth from contraction.

New orders rose at the fastest pace since March, while export orders increased only fractionally for a second straight month. Output also grew, but the pace eased from July's five-month high as material shortages constrained production.

Employment increased for a 21st consecutive month and at the sharpest pace since May 2025. Backlogs of work rose for the first time in three months, although the increase in outstanding business was only marginal.

Purchasing activity accelerated to its fastest since March as firms sought to build safety stocks. Supplier delivery times lengthened to the least marked degree since March, but S&P Global said vendor performance remained historically weak amid road transport issues.

Input cost inflation picked up in August, driven by higher energy, fuel and oil-derived material costs. Selling price inflation eased to its slowest since February, though it remained above the long-run average.

Manufacturers were more optimistic about the year-ahead outlook, with confidence rising to its highest since January 2024. Firms linked that to stronger order inflows, new client wins and investment in new premises.
